samples.summary: `saveSnapshot()` outside the new batch doubles every undo entry on `MemDocStore` — a dead Cmd+Z per edit
samples.evidence: Every new unit follows the shape `this.saveSnapshot(); this.withUndoUnit(() => {...})` (lines 814/816, 995/1001, 1532/1533, 2655/2656, 2695/2696, 4220/4221, plus `deleteSelection()`'s implicit unit at 3836 reached from 2483/2534/2583/2604/883/3408). `saveSnapshot` is wired to `docStore.snapshot()` (editor.ts:2475, text-box-editor.ts:680). `MemDocStore.snapshot()` only short-circuits when `batchDepth > 0` (store/memory.ts:181), and `MemDocStore.batch()` then pushes its OWN checkpoint unconditionally (store/memory.ts:206-209). So on the memory store one keystroke now leaves `undoStack = [..., A, A]`: the first Cmd+Z restores the pre-edit state, the second consumes an entry and changes nothing (and redo needs two presses too). The repo already spells this out: link-run.ts:81-85 — "`snapshot` … runs *inside* the batch … a call before the batch costs a second, identical undo step (a dead Cmd+Z)" — and `withNamedStyleChange` (editor.ts:1238-1239) puts `snapshot()` inside for exactly that reason. MemDocStore is the store for the slides text-box editor (text-box-editor.ts:431) and standalone docs mounts, so this is a live path. The Yorkie constraint (presence must be flushed outside the batch) is real, but it makes the two stores need different placement, which this change does not reconcile.

samples.summary: Holding interior `requestRender()` leaves the layout (and `blockParentMap`) stale for the rest of the undo unit; the paste path branches on it
samples.evidence: `render()` is synchronous — `recomputeLayout(); paint();` (editor.ts:2208-2211) — and `getLayout()` returns the `layout` variable that only `recomputeLayout()` reassigns (`invalidateLayout()` at editor.ts:1673 merely drops the cache, it does not refresh `layout`). Before this change, `deleteSelectionImpl`'s trailing `this.requestRender()` (lines 3910/3944/3995/4031/4060) refreshed the layout before the caller's remaining work ran. The new wrapper (718-724) swallows it until the outermost unit closes, so everything after `deleteSelection()` inside a unit now reads a PRE-delete layout. Concretely in `applyPastePlan` (1533-1539): `pasteTableCells` reads `this.getLayout().blockParentMap.get(pos.blockId)` (4416-4418) and `insertBlocks` reads `this.isInCell(pos.blockId)` (4291 → 3663, same map). The cell-range delete branch replaces each selected cell's blocks with FRESH ids (3927-3932) and parks the cursor on one of them (3938-3941); that id is absent from the stale map, so `cellInfo` is undefined, the code takes the "cursor not in a table" branch, `this.doc.getBlockIndex(pos.blockId)` returns -1 for a cell-internal block (model/document.ts:271-273) and `insertBlockAt(0, tableBlock)` (4436) drops the pasted table at the top of the body instead of into the cell that was just cleared. The mirror risk is a stale map that still resolves a *deleted* `tableBlockId`, where `this.doc.getBlock(tableBlockId)` (4445) throws (Doc.getBlock throws on a miss) inside the batch — under Yorkie that rolls the whole paste back.

samples.summary: `getWrapAffinity` after a batched `deleteSelection()` now resolves against the pre-delete layout
samples.evidence: `this.cursor.moveTo(newPos, this.getWrapAffinity(newPos))` (1027, and the same shape at 823 and 4269) runs inside the unit. `getWrapAffinity` → `getVisualLineRange` → `getActiveLayout()` (4682, 4729), which is the stale layout now that `deleteSelection()`'s render is deferred. It degrades rather than throws (`if (!lb) return [0, 0]` at 4730), so the cost is a wrong caret line-affinity — the caret can render on the wrong side of a wrap boundary — after typing/pasting over a selection that changed block structure.

samples.summary: The replayed render is always the full `requestRender`, losing the no-cursor-scroll / caret-only variants
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s finally replays `this.requestRender()`, i.e. the host's `renderWithScroll` (editor.ts:2434). If a unit's interior ever wants the non-scrolling variant (`requestRenderNoCursorScroll`, used at 2249) the distinction is lost, and the viewport is pulled back to the caret. No current unit uses the variant, so this is latent.

samples.summary: `undoFloorMark` keeps a strong reference to an undo entry Yorkie has already evicted
samples.evidence: Once the 50-entry cap drops the floor entry, `undoFloorMark` still holds it (and its whole reverse-operation array) for the lifetime of the store, since nothing ever clears it — `canUndo()` (2977) just keeps getting `-1`. Harmless in size terms, but the field could be nulled when the lookup misses.

verdict.reason: Verified in code: MemDocStore.snapshot() (memory.ts:177-184) pushes an undo checkpoint whenever batchDepth === 0, and MemDocStore.batch() (memory.ts:199-210) unconditionally pushes its own checkpoint of the identical pre-edit state; the wroteNothing pop (memory.ts:230-236) only fires for empty bodies, so a real edit leaves two identical entries. The editor calls saveSnapshot() immediately before withUndoUnit() (text-editor.ts:814/816, 995/1001) and before deleteSelection()'s implicit unit (879/883 → 3836); withUndoUnit routes to doc.batch (text-editor.ts:3816 → document.ts:148). saveSnapshot is wired to docStore.snapshot() on a MemDocStore in both the slides text-box editor (text-box-editor.ts:431 and 680) and the standalone docs mount (editor.ts:1042, 2474-2487). undoFn (editor.ts:2316-2330) and MemDocStore.undo (memory.ts:157-161) pop exactly one entry with no dedupe, so the second Cmd+Z is dead and redo needs two presses. The repo's own comment at link-run.ts:81-85 describes precisely this failure mode, and withNamedStyleChange (editor.ts:1236-1240) places snapshot() inside the batch to avoid it. No test pins snapshot-before-batch behavior (memory.test.ts only exercises snapshots inside batch, 238-269). Real, in-lane (broken undo invariant / incorrect state), reachable in normal editing.

verdict.reason: Verified every step in the repository. `render()` is synchronous (`editor.ts:2208-2211`) and `layout` is only reassigned in `recomputeLayout` (`editor.ts:1532`); `invalidateLayout()` (`editor.ts:1673-1676`) only drops the cache, and the TextEditor's `getLayout` is `() => layout` (`editor.ts:2460`). The wrapper at `text-editor.ts:718-724` swallows every interior `requestRender()` while `undoUnitDepth > 0`, replaying only after the outermost `withUndoUnit` closes (`text-editor.ts:3813-3824`). `applyPastePlan` (`text-editor.ts:1533-1539`) runs `deleteSelection()` and the insert inside one open unit, so no layout refresh happens between them. The cell-range delete branch installs blocks with `generateBlockId()` and parks the caret on one (`text-editor.ts:3927-3941`), so `pasteTableCells`'s `this.getLayout().blockParentMap.get(pos.blockId)` (`text-editor.ts:4416-4418`) misses, taking the "not in a table" branch where `getBlockIndex` returns -1 for a cell-internal block (`model/document.ts:271-273`) and `insertBlockAt(0, tableBlock)` (`text-editor.ts:4435-4436`) drops the pasted table at the top of the body. The same stale-map dependency exists via `isInCell` (`text-editor.ts:3662-3664`, used at `4291`). Nothing refreshes layout mid-batch (`Doc.refresh` at `model/document.ts:123-125`; `MemDocStore.batch` at `store/memory.ts:186-209`). Real, reachable in normal use, and in the correctness lane.
